messages:
Carlos (Support): FYI customer acme-prod reporting repeated 504s to hosted inference around 2025-11-03 14:23 UTC. They gave a request id: req-01FZ3K7V9M. Need dedicated cluster pod + node logs and a quick curl repro to attach to the ticket.

Ajay (Oncall): Got it. Can you paste the full request id(s), exact time window, and a minimal curl we can run? Also which dedicated pool / tenant namespace?

Carlos (Support): Request ids: req-01FZ3K7V9M and req-01FZ3K7WAA (same timeframe). Time window ~14:22:30–14:24:00 UTC. Namespace `dedicated-acme`, example pod `dedicated-acme-gen-78c9b4f6b9-xtlz2` on node `gpu-n3-02`. Minimal curl they used (token redacted):

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n     -H "X-Request-ID: req-01FZ3K7V9M" \n     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n     -d '{"model":"redwood-2-7b","input":"Summarize the following..."}' \n     https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```

They said it hangs ~10s then 504. Sometimes it returns 200 with truncated output.

Maria (Infra): Thanks — rough repro. Can you exec into the pod and check if the app wrote any local traces? If you can get `curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/debug/trace?reqid=req-01FZ3K7V9M` from the pod that would be ideal. Also we'll need kubectl logs + node kernel logs and GPU metrics.

Carlos (Support): I tried `kubectl logs -n dedicated-acme dedicated-acme-gen-78c9b4f6b9-xtlz2` but logs truncated. I can run the debug trace endpoint:

```bash
kubectl exec -n dedicated-acme -c generator dedicated-acme-gen-78c9b4f6b9-xtlz2 -- \n  sh -c "curl -sS 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/debug/trace?reqid=req-01FZ3K7V9M' > /tmp/trace-req-01FZ3K7V9M.json"\nkubectl cp dedicated-acme/dedicated-acme-gen-78c9b4f6b9-xtlz2:/tmp/trace-req-01FZ3K7V9M.json ./trace-req-01FZ3K7V9M.json
```

Ajay (Oncall): Also grab the pod description and container restart history:

```bash
kubectl describe pod -n dedicated-acme dedicated-acme-gen-78c9b4f6b9-xtlz2
```

Sam (SRE): For the node side, we'll need: `journalctl -u kubelet --since "2025-11-03 14:00"` and `dmesg | tail -n 200` plus `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION,TEMPERATURE` (or the NVML query). If there's an Xid or kernel GPU error it'll show up in dmesg. Also check cgroup throttling/oom.

Maria (Infra): To simplify collection, run our support helper on the pod (it bundles logs, `kubectl describe`, container traces, and runs `nvidia-smi` on the node via a privileged job). Example: 

```bash
# from support jumpbox with kube creds
/support/tools/collect-debug-bundle --namespace dedicated-acme --pod dedicated-acme-gen-78c9b4f6b9-xtlz2 --reqid req-01FZ3K7V9M --upload s3://redwood-support-debug/acme/
```

The tool will produce a tarball and upload to our support bucket and print a presigned URL. If you can't run it, I'll run a privileged job and post the link.

Carlos (Support): Running it now, uploading...

infra-bot: debug-bundle/uploader started for 1756789123 (user=carlos)

infra-bot: debug-bundle completed: s3://redwood-support-debug/acme/1756789123-acme-dedicated-bundle.tar.gz
Presigned URL (valid 24h): https://presigned.redwood-s3.example/1756789123-acme-dedicated-bundle.tar.gz?X-Amz-SignedHeaders=...

Ajay (Oncall): Perfect. I'll attach that to the support ticket and try to replay the request locally against the same model + token scope. For the internal replay use this curl (internal endpoint):

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <INTERNAL_TOKEN>" \
     -H "X-Request-ID: replay-01FZ3" \
     -H "X-Tenant: acme" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"redwood-2-7b","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":512}' \
     https://internal-api.redwood.svc/v1/generate
```

Sam (SRE): Maria — can you grep the bundle for `Xid` and `OOM` and post kernel snippets if present? Also check node GPU driver version and whether there were any driver module reloads.

Maria (Infra): On it. Quick grep results from bundle log: `dmesg.log` contains `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:02:00): 31` at 14:23:07 UTC and `nvidia: GPU crash dump` lines. I'll extract the surrounding 50 lines and attach here.

Carlos (Support): Adding the presigned link and the kernel excerpt to the ticket, letting customer know we're investigating and will follow up within 2 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Ajay (Oncall): Next steps: SRE to triage GPU Xid root cause (driver/kernel/temps), infra to check node sustained load and any throttling, and support to confirm whether customer saw any retries or partial responses. If we confirm GPU crash, we'll plan node remediation and possible model fallbacks.

Maria (Infra): Confirmed driver 525.105.17 on node `gpu-n3-02`. NVML shows memory spike before Xid. I'll open an infra incident if we see recurring Xid across pods on that node.

Sam (SRE): Acknowledged. I'll attempt the local replay and attach the generator container logs with timestamps for the replay req id so we can correlate.

Carlos (Support): Thanks team — attaching to ticket now. If you need anything else from the customer (e.g., additional request ids or timestamps) I'll request them. :thumbsup:
